name: ZH03B laser dust sensor
description: Winsen laser-scattering particulate (dust) module with built-in fan: measures PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 in ug/m3 (0-1000 ug/m3, particles 0.3-10 um). Sends a 24-byte frame once a second over a 9600-baud UART (3.3 V logic) by default, can be switched to question-and-answer mode or put to sleep, and also has a PWM output for PM2.5. Runs on 4.9-5.5 V, under 120 mA. Sold as: Winsen ZH03B laser dust module with its 8-pin 1.25 mm cable (pins 1-8: VDD, GND, NC, RXD, TXD, NC, NC, PWM).
eli5: A tiny fan pulls air past a laser and counts the dust and smoke specks it sees, then tells your board how dirty the air is.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Pin 1: supply 5 V (4.9-5.5 V), up to 120 mA for the fan and laser

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: Pin 4: module serial input, 3.3 V TTL: wire to the board's UART TX; only needed to send commands (Q&A mode, sleep)

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: Pin 5: module serial output, 3.3 V TTL, 9600 baud: wire to the board's UART RX

pins.name: PWM
pins.description: Pin 8: PWM output, 3.3 V, 1 s period, PM2.5 = 1000 x TH / (TH + TL) ug/m3 (optional)

supplierQuery: Winsen ZH03B laser dust sensor PM2.5 module UART
buildNotes: The module has an 8-pin 1.25 mm connector, not breadboard pins: use its cable and jumper wires.
Power VDD from 5 V (4.9-5.5 V, up to 120 mA): it will not run from 3.3 V. The UART pins are 3.3 V TTL, so TXD goes straight into an ESP32 or Pico RX pin.
Cross the serial wires: module TXD (pin 5) -> board RX, module RXD (pin 4) -> board TX (RXD is only needed to send commands).

9600 baud 8N1. By default the module sends 42 4D 00 14 followed by nine 16-bit fields and a 16-bit checksum once a second: PM1.0 = bytes 11-12, PM2.5 = bytes 13-14, PM10 = bytes 15-16 (ug/m3). Checksum = 16-bit sum of bytes 1-22; drop frames that fail it.
Wait about 30 s after power-on before trusting readings. Keep the inlet and the fan outlet clear (2 cm) and out of strong drafts.
Leave pins 3, 6 and 7 unconnected. Do not remove the metal shield.

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
from zh03b import ZH03B

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RXD}), rx=Pin({TXD}))
sensor = ZH03B(uart)
while True:
    r = sensor.read()
    print('PM1=%d PM2.5=%d PM10=%d' % (r['pm1_0'], r['pm2_5'], r['pm10']))

test.title: Reports the PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 set on the sliders
